Multi-Asset Risk Premia · Bouchouev Replication

Strategy Return Shapes — Momentum, Carry & Value, All 20 Products

Extends the momentum-smile check to Carry and Value: does each strategy's monthly return, plotted against the underlying's own monthly return, form a smile (rewarded by big moves), a frown (rewarded by calm/chop), or no clear pattern? There's no book figure for Carry/Value here — this is a novel extension of the idea, not a replication of a specific Bouchouev claim.

Momentum
20 smile / 0 frown / 0 mixed
Carry
3 smile / 2 frown / 15 mixed
Value
6 smile / 2 frown / 12 mixed

Headline

Momentum is the only one of the three with a universal, clean shape — 20/20 products smile. Carry and Value are overwhelmingly MIXED (no reliable monotonic pattern either way) across most products, with only a handful of frowns and smiles scattered in, and generally much lower R² than Momentum's fit.

This is itself informative: Momentum's edge is mechanically tied to how big the market moves (trend-following almost by definition benefits from big moves and suffers in chop). Carry and Value's returns come from a different source — term-structure persistence and price-level deviation, not the size of the underlying's move — so there's no equally strong mechanical reason to expect a clean smile or frown from them, and the data agrees.
